title: h b l f
overview:
New sounds: h, b, l, f.
Four more letters. Most short words are open to you now.
Say the sound, not the letter name.
Join the sounds and read the word.
functions: Say the sound each new letter makes
Join sounds together to read a word
Break a word into sounds to write it
Read the new words out loud
Read the common words that phonics cannot sound out
learningPath: Words: the new sounds and the new words.
Patterns: the sounds, blending, and writing.
Write the letters and the words.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 7. Four more letters.
First. h. Just a breath. h.
Put your hand near your mouth.
Say h. Feel the air.
There is no voice in h. Only air.
Next. b. A pop from your lips. b.
Say it with me. b. b. b.
Careful. In b the line comes first.
Then the circle. That is b, not d.
Next. lll. Tongue behind your teeth.
Say it with me. lll. Hold it.
Last. fff. Teeth on your lip.
Say it with me. fff. Hold it.
Now join them.
h. a. t. Hat.
Say it with me. h-a-t. Hat.
Another. b. e. d. Bed.
And. lll. e. g. Leg.
And. fff. u. nnn. Fun.
Now count what you know.
You have sixteen letters.
Most short words are open to you.
Three tricky words. Of. Be. His.
Of sounds like ov. It does not follow the rule.
That is Unit 7.

grammar.title: The new sounds: h, b, l, f
grammar.explanation:
Each letter makes one sound.
Say the SOUND, not the letter name.
The name comes later and does not help you read.
grammar.rule:
h   as in h
b   as in b
l   as in l
f   as in f
grammar.workedExample:
You see the letter h.
1. Do not say its name.
2. Say its sound.
3. Say it two or three times.
4. Now find it in a word.
5. Say the sound again in the word.
grammar.mistake:
Saying the letter NAME breaks blending.
Em-ay-pee will never make map.
Mmm-aaa-p makes map.
grammar.practice:
Say the sound for each one.
1. h
2. b
3. l
4. f
grammar.answers:
Check yourself out loud.
Did you say a sound and not a name?
All right? Go on to the blending card.

grammar.title: Joining h, b, l, f into words
grammar.explanation:
This is reading.
Say each sound, then run them together.
Slow first. Fast comes on its own.
grammar.rule:
h - a - t      ->  hat
b - e - d      ->  bed
l - e - g      ->  leg
f - u - n      ->  fun

Sixteen letters known. Most words are open now.
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word hat.
1. Say the first sound.
2. Say the next.
3. Say the last.
4. Now run them together, faster.
5. That is the word.
grammar.mistake:
Do not mix b and d.
In b the line comes first.
The word bed helps: b looks left, d looks right.
grammar.practice:
Join the sounds and write the word.
1. h - a - t
2. b - e - d
3. l - e - g
4. f - u - n
5. b - a - t
6. h - o - t
grammar.answers:
1. hat
2. bed
3. leg
4. fun
5. bat
6. hot
Five or six right? You can read these.

grammar.title: Writing words with h, b, l, f
grammar.explanation:
Reading is joining. Writing is the other way.
Say the word. Break it into sounds. Write each one.
grammar.rule:
cat  ->  c - a - t  ->  write c, then a, then t

Say it.
Count the sounds.
Write one letter for each sound.
grammar.workedExample:
You want to write the word bed.
1. Say it out loud.
2. Break it: b - e - d.
3. How many sounds? Count them.
4. Write one letter for each.
5. Read it back to check.
grammar.mistake:
Do not remember the word as a picture.
Hear the sounds. Write one letter for each.
grammar.tip: Say it, count it, write it, read it back.
grammar.practice:
Write the word you hear.
1. leg
2. fun
3. bat
4. hot
5. lid
6. fan
grammar.answers:
1. leg
2. fun
3. bat
4. hot
5. lid
6. fan
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.title: Tricky words: of, be, his
grammar.explanation:
Some words do not follow the sounds.
You cannot work them out. You learn them by sight.
There are not many, and they are the commonest words.
grammar.workedExample:
You meet the word of.
1. Try the sounds first. Always try first.
2. It does not work.
3. So this is a tricky word.
4. Look at it. Say it. Look away. Say it.
5. Do that three times today.
grammar.mistake:
Do not guess from the first letter.
Look at the whole word, then say it.
grammar.practice:
Read these out loud, by sight.
1. of
2. be
3. his
grammar.answers:
There is no working out here.
Check: did you read each one without stopping?
Not yet? Look, say, look away, say. Three times a day.

readings.title: A Hot Day
readings.genre: A short text using known sounds
readings.setting: A flat, on a hot afternoon
readings.passage:
It is hot.
I get up and put the fan on.
I get a cup of pop.
I sit on the bed and I sip.
The fan hums. It is a big fan.
It is not so hot. It is fun.

comprehension.q: What is the first word in the text?
Read line two out loud. Did you stop in the middle?
comprehension.a: Any honest answer. Stopping is normal at first.

comprehension.q: Find a word with h in it.
comprehension.a: Any word from the text containing h.
comprehension.why: Look along each line for the letter.

comprehension.q: How many lines are in this text?
Read the text again, a little faster. Was it easier?
comprehension.a: Usually yes. The second reading is always easier.
comprehension.why: This is the point of reading it twice.

comprehension.q: Find a tricky word in the text.
comprehension.why: Tricky words are the ones sounds do not build.

comprehension.q: What does this notice ask you to do?
comprehension.a: b and d are still the same shape

comprehension.q: Do what the notice says. Did you manage it?
comprehension.why: The notice is a real instruction, not a text.

comprehension.q: Is there a word here you cannot read yet?
comprehension.a: Any honest answer. Say which one.
comprehension.why: Name the word you are stuck on. Then ask.

comprehension.q: Read the whole notice out loud, twice.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — The new sounds
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat each sound.
h
b
l
f
Say the SOUND, not the letter name.
Now say each one three times.
Tap the mic. Say them all.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: are they sounds, not names?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say one of the new sounds. Say it back.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Join the sounds
speaking.instructions:
Say each word two ways. Slow, then fast.
1. h - a - t ... hat
2. b - e - d ... bed
3. l - e - g ... leg
4. f - u - n ... fun
5. b - a - t ... bat
6. h - o - t ... hot
Tap the mic. Say all six both ways.
Check: did the slow one have separate sounds?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three sounds. Join them and say the word.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Read the list
speaking.instructions:
Read these out loud, straight down the list.
hat
bed
leg
fun
bat
hot
lid
fan
Do it twice. The second time, try not to stop.
Tap the mic. Read the list twice.
Check: was the second time easier?
speaking.tutor: Read the list to the tutor. Ask which words were not clear.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Say it, then write it
speaking.instructions:
For each word: say it, break it, write it.
1. leg
2. fun
3. bat
4. hot
5. lid
6. fan
Tap the mic. Say each word and its sounds.
Check: did you say the sounds before you wrote?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for a short word. Break it into sounds out loud.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — The tricky words
speaking.instructions:
Read these by sight. Do not sound them out.
of
be
his
Look. Say. Look away. Say again.
Tap the mic. Read them all.
Check: did you read each one without stopping?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say a tricky word. Say it back without spelling it.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Slow, then faster
speaking.instructions:
Read this word three times.
hat
First: sound by sound, very slow.
Second: a little faster.
Third: as one word.
Tap the mic. Read it three times.
Check: was the third one one word, not three?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to listen to your three readings. Ask which was best.

writing.title: Writing 1 — The new letters
writing.prompt:
Write each new letter five times.
Say its sound as you write it.
writing.model:
h h h h h
b b b b b
l l l l l
f f f f f
writing.criteria:
Each letter five times.
Each one sits on the line.
You said the sound as you wrote it.
writing.support: Write two letters only, five times each.
writing.extension: Now write each letter once without looking.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Words from their sounds
writing.prompt:
Say each word. Break it into sounds.
Write one letter for each sound.
writing.criteria:
Six words.
Each one spelled from its sounds.
You read each one back after writing it.
writing.extension: Now write one word nobody said to you.

hat
bed
leg
fun
bat
hot
lid
fan

Was the second reading faster than the first?
Stopping on a word is normal. Try it again and move on.

activities.instructions:

1. of
2. be
3. his
Look, say, look away, say.
activities.answers:

Check: each one read without stopping?
Not yet? Three times a day for three days.

quizzes.why: Say the sound. The letter name does not help you read.

quizzes.q: When you read, you say the ___.
The letter h is in the word ___.
quizzes.why: Look along the word for the letter.

quizzes.q: Join the sounds: h - a - t. The word is ___.
quizzes.why: The sounds in order make the word.

quizzes.q: Join the sounds: b - e - d. The word is ___.
quizzes.why: Say each sound, then run them together.
Say it, count the sounds, write one letter for each.

quizzes.q: How many sounds are in hat?
quizzes.why: Count what you HEAR. Letters and sounds are not always the same number.

quizzes.q: A tricky word is one you ___.
quizzes.why: Its parts break the rules. You learn the whole word.

quizzes.q: Before you decide a word is tricky, you should ___.
quizzes.why: Phonics first. Most words do follow the sounds.

quizzes.q: Which of these is a tricky word?
quizzes.why: The others can all be sounded out.

quizzes.q: You cannot read a word. What do you do first?
quizzes.why: Slower, not louder. Then try again.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

This is the rule the whole level rests on and the one adults break most, because many of them half-know the alphabet already. Em-ay-pee will never make map. Correct it every single time, kindly, and say why.

teacherNotes.type: Blending is a motor skill, not a fact
teacherNotes.note: A learner who understands blending perfectly still cannot do it until they have done it a few hundred times. Repetition here is not remediation; it is the lesson. Keep the pace up and come back tomorrow.

teacherNotes.type: Tricky words are taught, not worked out
teacherNotes.note: Try the sounds first, always — most English words do follow them. When they do not, the move is look, say, look away, say, three times a day. Do not let a learner grind at a word that cannot be decoded.

teacherNotes.type: Sixteen letters is the turning point
teacherNotes.note: After this unit most short English words can be decoded, and a learner who has been working word by word can suddenly read a short text. Point that out: it is the first moment the effort visibly pays, and it is worth naming.

teacherNotes.type: h has no voice in it
teacherNotes.note: It is air only. A learner who tries to add voice produces something closer to a throat sound. Hand near the mouth, feel the puff, nothing else.

assignment.title: Read and write the new words
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say the sound for each new letter.
Then read these words, slowly and then faster:
hat, bed, leg, fun, bat, hot
2. Write each new letter five times.
Then write four of the words from their sounds.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
